newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Fourth crewman dies after Singapore tanker fire.
newsitem.headline: Fourth crewman dies after Singapore tanker fire.

text.p: A fourth crewman has died after an oil tanker fire in Singapore harbour earlier this week, police said on Friday.
"The fourth crewman died this afternoon in the hospital," a police spokesman told Reuters.
One crewman was found dead on Thursday, the day after the fire, and a second on Friday morning. A third crewman who had been taken to hospital with severe burns also died on Friday.

The fatalities followed a blaze aboard the 26,909-dwt oil product tanker Ocean Trader on Wednesday. The Singapore-registered vessel was berthed at an oil terminal operated by the U.S. company Mobil Corp at the time.
"Everyone's been accounted for," an official from the tanker's owners, Ocean Tanker Pte Ltd, told Reuters.
Mobil said the tanker had been discharging condensate, a type of light crude oil, to the Mobil refinery when the fire broke out. The cause of the blaze was not known.
"We are waiting for the green light to discharge the cargo," the Ocean Tanker official said.
